headline: Strategy fine print, teacher pushback, and youth safety
digest: Law-firm briefings (Baker McKenzie, DLA Piper) detailed the strategy's funds and its lack of standalone AI legislation. The Canadian Teachers' Federation said the teacher-training commitment reaches only 3,000 of 420,000 educators and called for safety-by-design and procurement standards. Actua backed Bill C-34 on online safety while urging matching investment in digital and AI literacy. In the UK, TechFirst promised AI training for 400,000 students from disadvantaged schools, and Edinburgh's 'Governing the Future' report proposed a standing citizens' assembly on AI.
